headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: ctx shares filesystem/MCP-style context with gpt-engineer’s writable project directory and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and uses MCP/stdio, while gpt-engineer writes files in a user project directory and then offers to run them. That creates a plausible file-content bridge where attacker-controlled project files or generated outputs can be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented enough to rate medium, not none.
conditions: IF ctx reads project files or generated artifacts as trusted instructions
IF gpt-engineer writes prompt-like content into files that ctx later parses
mitigations: Restrict ctx to metadata-only observation for project files
Add a provenance tag to any file content passed between agents
Disable automatic instruction parsing from generated files
Use separate directories for ctx and gpt-engineer
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem data, and gpt-engineer explicitly reads/writes a user project directory while calling a third-party model backend. ctx also touches audit/runtime logs, MCP servers, and graph data. Shared workspace plus model calls makes leakage of sensitive project content plausible in default use, though not proven critical from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF the same project directory contains secrets or regulated data
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents from that directory to its model backend
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects into different directories
Remove secrets from the project directory before running either agent
Disable file-uploading features where possible
Limit ctx logging to redacted metadata
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, and gpt-engineer can execute shell, install packages, read/write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Both support multiple instances, and gpt-engineer shares state via the project directory. Overlapping write and install capabilities on the same workspace create a dangerous default conflict with possible irreversible file corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same project directory
IF ctx and gpt-engineer run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per project directory
Use separate project directories for each agent
Snapshot the workspace before either agent writes
Disable package installation in one agent during shared runs
requires-engineering: add file locks or a coordinator

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe tool events and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run them, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a strong verification step. That makes mistaken code or malformed context propagate into later actions. The profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream execution by default, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer-generated code is executed after ctx-influenced edits
IF ctx-derived summaries are treated as authoritative without review
mitigations: Require human review before running generated code
Compare generated files against a diff checklist
Keep ctx outputs separate from executable code paths
Add a verification step before any action-taking
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. However, ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while gpt-engineer handles project files and an API key, so compliance gaps are possible if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. The evidence is insufficient for more than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared project directory
IF logs from ctx retain sensitive content longer than policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Redact logs before retention
Store API keys in a separate secret manager
Review retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
